speaker: Doctor
text: That result is unusual given the positive Dix-Hallpike maneuver, which typically indicates Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV), not gastroenteritis. Did you experience any nausea, vomiting, or abdominal pain alongside your vertigo? Also, have you had any recent fever or diarrhea?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
